objections.q: Can't you just get us reviews?
objections.a: No one honest can. Paying or trading for reviews breaks Google's policy and the FTC's rule. What works is asking every customer, every time, with one tap.

objections.q: I only want the happy customers to review.
objections.a: I get it, but asking only happy customers is against Google's policy and could break the FTC Act. Ask everyone, and reply to every review: a calm reply to a bad review shows the next customer how you treat people.
Then the card makes it one tap instead of a search. Check the date of your newest review: if it's months old, the ask isn't reaching people.
Most people read reviews, and a code at the counter makes it a 30-second job while they're still there.

objections.q: What if someone leaves a bad review?
objections.a: Every good shop gets one. A calm reply within a day shows the next customer how you treat people, and a steady stream of recent reviews puts one bad day in context. I draft a reply to every review for you.

objections.q: We don't have time for this.
objections.a: It takes almost none of yours: the card sits on the counter, the line goes on the receipt, and I draft every reply. Your team's part is one sentence at checkout.
Fair. Review software alone often runs $49 to $125 a month, and it doesn't put a card in your customer's hand or draft your replies. Try the first month, and cancel any month.
